options.why: A large population is one of the conditions for equilibrium.

options.why: A blocked receptor cannot trigger the pathway, so glucose release is not triggered.

options.why: A drug that blocks the receptor does not activate it, so the response is not increased.

options.why: Adds the two times instead of dividing one by the other.

items.stem: A third treatment places the leaf disks in very dim light, much dimmer than the dim light treatment. Which prediction is best supported by the data and by the process of photosynthesis?

options.text: Disks would float sooner than in bright light, because plants make more oxygen in the dark.
options.why: Photosynthesis needs light and does not make more oxygen in the dark.

options.text: Disks would float even later than in dim light, because less light energy would drive the light reactions and oxygen production would be slower.
options.why: Less light reduces the output of the light reactions, so less oxygen collects in the disks per minute.

options.text: Disks would float at the same time as in dim light, because light has no effect on oxygen production.
options.why: The data show that light intensity affects the floating time.

options.text: Disks would float only if carbon dioxide were removed from the solution.
options.why: Removing carbon dioxide would reduce photosynthesis and delay floating.

ap_biology-m13.set_intro: A student places leaf disks in bicarbonate solution under two light intensities and counts how many of ten disks float over time. Disks float when oxygen from photosynthesis collects inside them. The table shows the data.

stimulus.description: Number of leaf disks floating (out of 10) over time at two light intensities

items.stem: Which statement best describes the data in the table?

options.text: More disks floated sooner in dim light than in bright light.
options.why: The table shows more disks floating in bright light at each early time.

options.text: More disks floated sooner in bright light than in dim light.
options.why: In bright light 9 disks were floating at 8 minutes, compared with 1 in dim light.

options.text: The same number of disks floated at each time in both light intensities.
options.why: The numbers of floating disks differ between the two light intensities.

options.text: No disks floated in either light intensity.
options.why: Disks floated in both light intensities.

items.stem: Assuming a steady change between measurements, what is the best estimate of the time at which half of the disks had floated in bright light?

options.text: 6.0 minutes
options.why: Reports the first measured time at which more than five disks had floated in bright light.

options.text: 11.0 minutes
options.why: Reports the time for the dim light treatment.

options.text: 5.0 minutes
options.why: Five disks is half of ten. Between 4 minutes (3 disks) and 6 minutes (7 disks), the time is estimated by interpolation: 5.0 minutes.

options.text: 4.0 minutes
options.why: Reports the last measured time before more than five disks had floated in bright light.
